TVB-O: Description back to ToC

TVB-O, The Virtual Brain Ontology, describes large-scale brain network models and their simulation: neural mass and neural field models with their parameters, state variables and equations, coupling functions, connectomes and brain atlases, integrators and noise, observation models, and the simulation experiments and studies that combine them. Every model, network and experiment curated in the TVB-O database is an individual of the ontology at https://w3id.org/tvbo//.

Cross-reference for TVB-O classes, object properties and data properties back to ToC

This section provides details for each class and property defined by TVB-O.

Analysisc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Analysis

A quantity obtained by analysing a model, its solve, a derived loss, simulated results, or empirical data — as opposed to transforming a recorded trajectory. Analysing a solve is named by Analysis.type (see AnalysisObservable); analysing saved data is named by the callable invoked over the arrays it used.
A quantity obtained by ANALYZING something — a model, its solve, a derived loss, simulated results, or empirical data — rather than by transforming a recorded trajectory. Nothing here requires a model: decomposing empirical maps into a basis, taking their spectrum, or running a permutation test over measured data are analyses in exactly this sense, and so are parameter sensitivities/gradients (autodiff or finite-difference), stability spectra (Lyapunov), bifurcation quantities, identifiability metrics, and reductions spanning several experiments. It is an invocation (``is_a: FunctionCall``) with two mutually exclusive ways of saying WHAT is analyzed, the same alternative-specification idiom ``Parameter`` uses for provenance: - **the solve** — ``type`` names the analysis (a free string, extensible; the vocabulary lives in the ontology as AnalysisObservable concepts rather than a closed enum), ``target`` and ``wrt`` bind it to what is analyzed and with respect to what, and ``parameters`` configures it. Evaluated as part of the integration, so it is emitted by the same codegen and limited to what that backend can trace. Declared on ``Observation.analysis``. - **saved data** — ``callable`` (or ``class_call``) invoked with ``arguments``, each a literal ``value`` or a ``used:`` DataRef reading an experiment, another analysis, or a dataset. The data need not be simulated: this is equally the form for analysing empirical maps, an atlas, or a measured connectome. Because it consumes containers rather than a running solve, it is scheduled on its own — before or after the experiments, according to what it uses. Declared in ``SimulationStudy.analyses``, where the result is persisted as its own container (``derivatives/tvbo/ana-<name>_result.h5``) — which is what lets a figure bind it with ``used: {analysis: <name>}`` exactly as it binds a run, and why a study needs no driver script for its non-simulation figures. ``name`` is then required and unique, since it keys that container. The invocation yields a mapping of name -> labelled array (or one array, keyed by the analysis name); each key becomes an ``observation__<key>`` data-variable keeping its dims and coordinates, so a figure ``encoding`` can name them. Like a ``SimulationExperiment``, an Analysis declares its own ``execution``: which backend renders it, at what precision, on which accelerator. That states a requirement, not a mechanism — the same analysis is renderable by more than one backend, and one that cannot render it says so rather than silently substituting another.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
FunctionCall c

Argumentc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Argument

A function argument with explicit value specification. A value is either ``value`` (a literal / array / local reference) or ``used`` (a labelled array sourced from another experiment or dataset); the two are mutually exclusive. Value can be: literal (number/string), reference to input (input.key), or cross-observation reference (observation_name.output_key). A bare scalar is the value, as it is for a Parameter: ``sel: {variable: phi}`` and ``opts: {xlabel: "time (s)"}`` mean ``{value: …}``, which is how both are written throughout the docs.

Assignmentc back to ToC or Class ToC

One step of a sequential recurrence: the expression assigned to a target name. Sequential rather than simultaneous — a later step's expression sees the value the steps above it assigned — which is what lets a reducer's update be authored as ordinary arithmetic instead of with `new_*` temporaries. Authored terse as a `[target, expression]` pair and lifted to this form on load.

https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

AxisReductionc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/AxisReduction

Marks an exploration/sweep axis to be collapsed by a statistic in the result container. When set on an ExplorationAxis, that axis's named grid dimension is reduced across every observation that carries it (e.g. an `execution.random_seed` trial ensemble becomes a first-class reduced observation). Backend-independent: states the reduction intent; the result layer applies it by dimension name.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

AxisReductionStatisticc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/AxisReductionStatistic

Statistic used to collapse an exploration/sweep axis into a single reduced value in the result container (see ExplorationAxis.reduce). Applied across the named grid dimension of every observation that carries it.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
is equivalent to
mean (AxisReductionStatistic) c or median (AxisReductionStatistic) c or sem (AxisReductionStatistic) c or std (AxisReductionStatistic) c or sum (AxisReductionStatistic) c
has super-classes
Thing c
has sub-classes
mean (AxisReductionStatistic) c, median (AxisReductionStatistic) c, sem (AxisReductionStatistic) c, std (AxisReductionStatistic) c, sum (AxisReductionStatistic) c

Cohort (study)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/study/Cohort

A named subset of a dataset's subjects: the unit a group-level quantity is defined over, such as a mean connectome, a per-edge presence count or a normalisation constant. A dataset may hold several, and they may overlap: the sites of a multi-centre study, a patient and a control group, the subjects a processing pipeline has finished so far. Naming the subset is what pins an aggregate. A quantity computed over ``hcpy93`` states which subjects went into it, and moving to a larger cohort is a change to one identifier rather than to every consumer.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

CohortRule (study)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/study/CohortRule

Admits a cohort's members by a measure of a phenotype table: the candidates are cut into ``n_groups`` groups along ``measure`` and the cohort holds the group ``group``. The candidates are the members of the cohort ``of`` names, else the subjects the dataset lists, else every subject of the table. Each candidate needs one row in the table. A candidate without a row, or whose value is missing or not finite, is treated as ``missing`` says, before any group is formed. The members come in the candidates' order, not in the order of the measure. A group no candidate falls in is an error, as a cohort without members is.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

Colorbarc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Colorbar

The colour scale a panel prints beside its field. Declared as one object because nine loose `colorbar_*` options were nine chances to style a bar that is not drawn, and because a tick list written in an options bag is not a list of numbers to anything that reads it. A heatmap carries one unasked, since it is unreadable without one; a scatter shaded by a third quantity asks with `show: true`, because a row of them conventionally shares ONE bar. `kind: colorbar` is the standalone form — a bar occupying its own cell of the mosaic, keying the panels around it, and the only case that states its own `colormap` and limits rather than taking them from the field it sits beside.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/PanelKind#colorbar

A colour scale in its own slot, for panels that share one. Attaching it to any single panel steals that panel's width and implies the scale is local to it. Limits come from opts or, with a layer bound, from the data. Built in.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
PanelKind c

Colormapsc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Colormaps

Continuous colour scales, by key: anything ordinal or continuous draws from one of these, anything categorical draws from `Palette.palette`, and an ordinal scale drawn as discrete swatches samples one rather than picking hues that imply no order. A value is either a registered colormap name (`viridis`) or the list of colours to ramp between (`['#000000', '#ffffff']`). The namespace is open — a project adds its own keys for the scales it distinguishes (`bold: viridis, meg: plasma, eeg: cividis`) and names them anywhere a colormap is named. `sequential` and `diverging` are the two the renderer reaches for on its own, so they are typed here and always present: a project that declares neither still has both. An open namespace cannot catch a misspelt key — `sequentiel` is read as a project key, not as a typo — which is the price of letting a project name its own scales. A key that shadows a registered colormap name is refused, so a name cannot mean two things at once.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

ColorScalec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/ColorScale

How values become colours, and where the scale starts and stops. Shared by everything that paints a field rather than drawing marks — a colour bar, a cortical surface, a labelled volume, a connectome — so the same question is answered with the same words wherever it is asked, and a limit means the same thing on all four. Every slot here reaches all four; a scale concern only one of them can answer is declared on that one, which is why `center` sits on `Colorbar`.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c
has sub-classes
Colorbar c, Graph c, Surface c, Volume c

CouplingStageEvaluationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/CouplingStageEvaluation

How the network coupling term is evaluated within one step of a multi-stage integrator (Heun, RK4, ...). A backend-neutral numerical contract: whether the coupling is part of the vector field, re-evaluated at each solver stage, or computed once per step and held constant across the stages. Matters because the two choices integrate a different effective system — for stiff / chaotic / multistable dynamics they can converge to different trajectories or attractors.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
is equivalent to
per_stage (CouplingStageEvaluation) c or per_step (CouplingStageEvaluation) c
has super-classes
Thing c
has sub-classes
per_stage (CouplingStageEvaluation) c, per_step (CouplingStageEvaluation) c

DataRefc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/DataRef

A pointer to one labelled array in a result container, dataset, or curated entity — the single cross-container reference primitive (a PROV entity a consumer ``prov:used``). WHERE is ``experiment`` (an in-study experiment id, resolved like ``initial_state.source_experiment``), ``analysis`` (an in-study analysis name), ``cohort`` (a named subset of a study dataset, read from each member's own file chosen by ``query``), or the full ``iri`` (a curated / result / external pointer); at most one. An ``iri`` that names a network, by the path of its sidecar file or by a curated network's exact id, reads ``output`` as a layer of that network (an edge layer or a per-node quantity) as the network delivers it, its own sources read and its transforms applied. WHICH is ``output`` (a recorded variable, ``observation__<name>``, ``estimate__<param>``, an external variable, or the measure a cohort member's file holds). SLICE is ``sel`` (label-keyed ``.sel``, never positional). ``reconcile`` optionally aligns the sourced array to the consuming network's node order by label. One model reused by figure layers (``Layer.used``), sourced arguments (``Argument.used``), sourced parameters (``Parameter.used``) and sourced network layers (``Edge.used``), so data binding, cross-experiment sourcing and PROV provenance are the same edge. A sourced array is resolved lazily and never inlined into generated code.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

Differentiationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Differentiation

Backend-neutral configuration for how gradients are propagated through the temporal integration. Expressed in physical/semantic terms; each backend maps it to its own mechanism (JAX solver grad_horizon / block_size, Julia adjoint sensitivity, ...). Backends without autodiff (e.g. MATLAB) emit a comment noting differentiation is unsupported and proceed with the plain forward integration -- they do not raise.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

Digestc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Digest

One checksum of an artifact, keyed by the function that produced it. Collected on ``Provenance.digest``, whose collection KEY is the function name — BEP028 takes the names ``MD5``, ``SHA1``, ``SHA-256`` and the rest of that list, and allows an arbitrary label otherwise. Keyed rather than a bare string so an artifact can carry several digests and a reader knows which function to check with.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

DistributionConfigc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/DistributionConfig

Policy for mapping a parameter sweep's exploration axes onto the two parallelism tiers when rendering a distributed workflow. Vectorized axes are packed into a single batched backend call (e.g. vmap/pmap); workflow axes are fanned out into independent scheduler tasks, one per value combination. Backend-independent: the emitter validates that a requested vectorized axis is one the chosen backend can actually batch.

https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

Documentc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Document

The envelope of a record written as its own file. ``tvbo_class`` names the class the file holds and ``schema_version`` the schema it was written against; both are facts about the file, so TVBO's dialect drops them before construction and no object ever carries them. Declaring them here is what lets a third party validate a TVBO file with plain ``linkml-validate``. A class taking this mixin pins its own CURIE with ``slot_usage: {tvbo_class: {equals_string: ...}}``, so a file naming the wrong class is refused natively.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c
has sub-classes
ExperimentResultSidecar c, Network c, Phenotype c, Theme c

DomainEnforcementc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/DomainEnforcement

Whether and how a state variable's ``domain`` constrains the trajectory during integration. Default ``none`` means the domain is descriptive metadata only (expected range, plot limits, initial- condition sampling support) and never alters the dynamics — so declaring a domain is side-effect free. ``clamp`` and ``wrap`` opt in to active enforcement using the domain's ``lo``/``hi``.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
is equivalent to
clamp (DomainEnforcement) c or none (DomainEnforcement) c or wrap (DomainEnforcement) c
has super-classes
Thing c
has sub-classes
clamp (DomainEnforcement) c, none (DomainEnforcement) c, wrap (DomainEnforcement) c

equal_count (CohortGrouping)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/CohortGrouping#equal_count

Groups of equal size by rank. The candidates are ordered by ascending value, equal values in the candidates' own order, and that order is cut into ``n_groups`` consecutive runs whose sizes differ by at most one, the longer runs first. Equal values can therefore fall into neighbouring groups.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
CohortGrouping c

equal_width (CohortGrouping)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/CohortGrouping#equal_width

Bins of equal width. The range from the smallest to the largest finite value among the candidates is cut into ``n_groups`` intervals of the same width; each is closed below and open above, and the last is closed on both sides, so the largest value belongs to it. Group sizes follow the distribution of the measure and a bin may hold nobody. Refused when all values are equal and more than one group is asked for, since the range then has no width.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
CohortGrouping c

A continuation from a special point of another is declared as a branch of that continuation instead (Continuation.branches, with its BranchSwitch.source_point).
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
InitialStateMethod c

from_experiment (InitialStateMethod)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/InitialStateMethod#from_experiment

Seed from the settled endpoint state of another already-run experiment in the study (referenced by InitialState.source_experiment). Reuses a working point that experiment already reached instead of recomputing it — the cross-experiment counterpart of from_working_point (which recomputes the ramp inline). source_point selects which settled point of the source run (default 'endpoint').
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
InitialStateMethod c

from_previous (SweepSeeding)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/SweepSeeding#from_previous

Each point is seeded from the final state of the preceding point, so the trajectory follows the solution branch as the swept parameter changes quasi-statically. Forces sequential, order-dependent execution (emitted as a scan, not a vmap). Used to reach a working point by slowly ramping a parameter (e.g. global coupling) and, with sweep_direction, to expose hysteresis / multistability. The sweep-granularity form of InitialStateMethod.from_working_point, which ramps a parameter to one working point.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
SweepSeeding c

from_working_point (InitialStateMethod)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/InitialStateMethod#from_working_point

Ramp a parameter quasi-statically (warm-start / from_previous) to a target value (see InitialState.ramp) and start from the endpoint state — reach a working point on the solution branch before the run.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
InitialStateMethod c

FunctionCallc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/FunctionCall

Invocation of a function in a pipeline. Can reference a defined Function by name, OR inline a callable directly for external library functions, OR inline an equation, OR use class_call for class instantiation, OR name a curated step with `iri` and state only what differs from it. Mirrors Function attributes so pipeline steps can be self-contained. The `name` is an optional step label (used in pipelines for keyed access to step outputs); it is NOT a global identifier (singleton uses like `loss`, `observable` may omit it).

GraphRepresentationc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/GraphRepresentation

How a Network's connectivity is represented when evaluating coupling. This is a backend-independent performance contract, not a numerical one: both representations compute the same coupling, but a sparse representation sums over the existing edges (cost scales with the number of edges) while a dense representation operates on the full adjacency (cost scales with nodes-squared). A backend maps the choice onto its own primitives (edge gather / segment-sum vs matrix product). Orthogonal to whether the coupling reads *delayed* states — that is decided per coupling by its conduction delay — so the two dimensions together yield the four backend graph kinds: dense/sparse × instantaneous/delayed.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
is equivalent to
auto (GraphRepresentation) c or dense (GraphRepresentation) c or sparse (GraphRepresentation) c
has super-classes
Thing c
has sub-classes
auto (GraphRepresentation) c, dense (GraphRepresentation) c, sparse (GraphRepresentation) c

Gridc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Grid

How a `grid` panel tiles its cells, and what the strips around them are labelled with. Rows and columns are labelled ONCE, at the left and the top — the whole reason a paper's composite panel is one lettered panel rather than n of them. The reserved label strips are taken out of the drawable area, so declaring one shrinks the cells to make room instead of being drawn over them. The axis labels the cells SHARE are the panel's own `xlabel`/`ylabel`, one word at two levels, not slots of this object. A directive that varies down the rows or across the columns is still written as `row.<name>` / `col.<name>` in `opts`: it supplies one value per row or column of ANY directive, so it cannot be a fixed slot of anything.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

grid (PanelKind)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/PanelKind#grid

A composite of sub-panels inside ONE lettered panel, labelled once per row and column. What a paper's lettered panel usually is: a row of mode surfaces under a single (a), or a Data/Reconstruction matrix whose task name is written once at the left. Declaring each cell as its own mosaic entry instead would repeat those labels in every cell and renumber panels the paper letters once. Cells come from `cells:` or, in the common case, from `layers:` — one cell per layer, all drawn by the shared `cell:` template.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
PanelKind c

independent (SweepSeeding)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/SweepSeeding#independent

Points are order-independent and may be evaluated in parallel (see parallel_mode). Default. Independent of each OTHER, which is not the same as each cold-starting: where the experiment declares a transient, the settle is integrated once and every point opens from the state it reached, so what is shared between points is a settled state rather than a running trajectory. That is sound while the swept parameter does not change the approach, and unsound wherever the sweep crosses a bifurcation, since a point then inherits an attractor it would not have reached on its own. The emitter integrates one settle, not one per point, so the name promises independence between points, not a cold start at each.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
SweepSeeding c

Inferencec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Inference

Bayesian inference of model parameters from an observation, via MCMC. A standalone, first-class concept (NOT an Optimization): it produces a POSTERIOR, not a point estimate, using priors + a likelihood + a sampler instead of a loss + optimizer. It runs the SAME differentiable forward model, wrapped in a probabilistic model (sample priors -> forward -> likelihood).
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

LayoutEnginec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/LayoutEngine

Which matplotlib layout engine positions the mosaic's axes. Unset lets the backend pick (bsplot asks for 'compressed' and falls back to 'tight'), which is right for a plain grid of plots. A figure whose panels carry their own absolute geometry — a schematic stepped out in axes fractions, or a mosaic dense enough that the constrained solver reports cells collapsed to zero and silently falls back — has to say so, because an engine that gives up still leaves the figure laid out by a fallback nobody declared.

Legendc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Legend

A panel's key: whether it is drawn, where it sits, and the three things a figure actually asks of one beyond that. An object rather than a bare position because `frame` had nowhere to live — the renderer drew every key frameless whatever the theme said, so a theme asking for a boxed legend never got one. The shorthands are the same slot: `legend: true` is `{show: true}` and `legend: upper right` is `{loc: upper right}`, expanded on load, so a panel that starts with a corner and later needs two columns keeps the word it had. Distinct from `kind: legend`, which is a standalone legend PANEL occupying a cell of the mosaic and sharing no axes with anything.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

legend (PanelKind)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/PanelKind#legend

A key in its own slot, for a convention several panels share. Entries are parallel `labels`/`colors`/`linestyles` lists. Built in.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
PanelKind c

Where a panel's key sits. `best` lets the backend find the emptiest corner, which is right while a figure is still moving and wrong once it is printed — a key that relocates between two renders of the same figure is a difference the spec never stated.

has sub-classes
best (LegendLoc) c, center (LegendLoc) c, center left c, center right c, lower center c, lower left c, lower right c, right (LegendLoc) c, upper center c, upper left c, upper right c

Likelihoodc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Likelihood

Observation model for Bayesian inference: p(data | sim(theta)). Points at the observation holding the data and specifies the noise family + scale. `name` is the noise family (default Normal); `source` uses the same referencing as `Observation.source`, so the observed data can come from this experiment's integration, an empirical network measure, or a runtime-bound array — one flexible hook, no data-loading path of its own. `predicted` names the other side of the residual when it differs from the data's own observable.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

Meshc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Mesh

Triangle (or higher-order) mesh geometry. May stand alone (via ``mesh_file`` pointing at an external GIFTI/VTK/MSH file) OR be inlined on a Network as ``Network.mesh``. In the inlined-on-Network case, the vertices are the parent Network's ``nodes/coordinates`` (so ``coordinates`` here may be left empty), the faces live in the same h5 companion under a path given by ``elements`` (default ``mesh/faces``), and optional per-vertex ``normals`` / ``curvature`` live alongside. The optional ``parcel_map_field`` points at the parent Network's per-vertex parcel-id array (default ``nodes/parent_index`` from the hierarchical-Network pattern, see Network.qmd §7.1).

https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

nested (AlgorithmCompositionMode)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/AlgorithmCompositionMode#nested

The included algorithm runs as a full inner loop on EACH outer iteration, re-converging before the outer update rules are applied. Use when the inner algorithm maintains an invariant the outer one would otherwise perturb — e.g. FIC holding the E-I working point (mean S_e = 0.25) while EIB retunes per-edge coupling. The outer update's validity depends on that invariant, so the inner loop must re-settle it between every outer step.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
AlgorithmCompositionMode c

network (PanelKind)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/PanelKind#network

The connectome as a node-link graph: one marker per region at its anatomical centre, edges drawn for the connections that survive `edge_percentile`. A layer supplies one value per region and colours the markers with it, so what the panel shows is a state living ON the network rather than beside it. Geometry comes from the `network:` the panel names, values are placed BY LABEL through the node labels, and `projection` picks the anatomical plane the centres flatten onto. Needs no code_modules — the drawing is built in.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
PanelKind c

NodeSelectionc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/NodeSelection

The nodes of a network to keep or to drop, by label; exactly one of ``keep`` and ``drop`` is stated. A label is matched as written or through the aliases a ``by_label`` reconciliation uses (a node's ``alternateName`` and the atlas terminology). A selection is a set: the kept nodes stay in the order the network carries them, whatever order ``keep`` lists them in, and are renumbered from 0. The selection is applied when the network is resolved, after its source has delivered nodes and arrays and before anything else reads them. Every stored layer, edge-parameter matrix and per-node array (``nodes/<name>``) is restricted to the kept nodes, an edge listed between two nodes goes with either of its nodes, and ``number_of_nodes`` is the kept count. Transforms, delays and couplings therefore see the selected network only: a normalisation by the largest weight is taken over the kept pairs. A layer or argument read through ``used:`` is read for the selected nodes: with ``reconcile: by_label`` it is aligned to them by name, without it the array has to come in the selected node count. A layer a ``producer:`` builds is not cut and has to come in the selected node count, and a per-node parameter read by ``source`` and ``measure`` from a network with more nodes is aligned to the kept nodes by label. A warning names the network and both counts whenever a selection drops nodes from what the network carries; read back beside arrays that are already the selected ones, it drops none and gives none. Refused, naming what is wrong: a label the network does not carry, ``keep`` beside ``drop``, a label listed twice, a selection that leaves no node, a node declared by label that the selection drops, and a network that carries a mesh or a route to another network, whose arrays the selection cannot restrict.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

ObservationReductionModec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/ObservationReductionMode

How an observation is evaluated over the trajectory (see Observation.reduce). Absent (the default) keeps the post-scan pipeline: the observation is computed from a materialised trajectory. `streaming` opts the observation into an incremental reducer that is folded into the integrator carry via prepare(reduce=...), so the trajectory is never held — byte-identical to the post-scan value (to f64 rounding), but with O(block) instead of O(n_time) peak memory. Required for whole-brain fits whose per-stage simulation is long enough that the full trajectory would not fit in memory (e.g. the Schirner 2023 BOLD/FC group fit).
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
is equivalent to
streaming (ObservationReductionMode) c or trials (ObservationReductionMode) c
has super-classes
Thing c
has sub-classes
streaming (ObservationReductionMode) c, trials (ObservationReductionMode) c

Palettec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Palette

A project's colours, named by role. The colour half of a `Theme`, and a document in its own right for a consumer that wants colours and nothing else (:mod:`tvbo.plot.palette`, the documentation site's stylesheet). A style sheet carries only what matplotlib has an rcParam for, which stops short of the roles a figure reasons in: the one colour that means *this is the point*, the neutral everything unlabelled is drawn in, the hairline behind it. Naming them here is what makes recolouring a project one edit that every panel follows. The cycler is `[base] + palette`, so a plot that names no colour comes out neutral and only a panel meaning to separate conditions reaches into the hues; `highlight` sits outside the cycler, because a colour handed to the second line of every plot cannot also mean emphasis. TVB-O's own is curated at `tvbo:themes/default`, and is the palette in force until a project names one of its own.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c
has sub-classes
Theme c

per_stage (CouplingStageEvaluation)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/CouplingStageEvaluation#per_stage

Re-evaluate the coupling at every integrator stage, as part of the vector field: standard ODE integration, and what a reference integrator of a stiff, chaotic or multistable network computes. tvboptim's native solvers honour it as recompute_coupling_per_stage=True, NetworkDynamics.jl integrates this way natively, and the jax backend re-evaluates an undelayed coupling at each stage's state and refuses it over a delayed one, whose history read it cannot shift to a stage's time. TVB and the Python graph runner compute the coupling once per step, so they refuse it wherever it changes the system integrated: a multi-stage method over more than one node. tvboptim's diffrax solvers and PyRates integrate this way whatever is declared.
Alternative label
per_stage
recompute_coupling_per_stage
scope note
Re-evaluate the network coupling term at every stage of a multi-stage integrator. Costlier, but the coupling seen by each stage is consistent with that stage's state; the difference from per-step matters for stiff or chaotic coupled networks.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
CouplingStageEvaluation c

per_step (CouplingStageEvaluation)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/CouplingStageEvaluation#per_step

Evaluate the coupling once per integration step and hold it across the step's stages, the TVB scheme: the coupling reduction runs once per step, at the cost of an order of accuracy in the coupling, which can move a sensitive system onto another trajectory. TVB and the Python graph runner always integrate this way, and the jax backend and tvboptim's native solvers do as their default (recompute_coupling_per_stage=False on tvboptim). NetworkDynamics.jl holds each vertex's summed input on parameters that a callback sets at the start of every step, for every multi-stage method, adaptive ones included, and refuses it together with execution.find_fixpoint. tvboptim's diffrax solvers and PyRates re-evaluate the coupling at every stage whatever is declared.
Alternative label
per_step
scope note
Evaluate the network coupling once per integration step and hold it frozen across the integrator's stages. The default, and the classic TVB treatment.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
CouplingStageEvaluation c

Phenotypec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Phenotype

Per-subject phenotype table (BIDS ``phenotype/`` directory convention). Carries cognitive scores, clinical scales, demographic variables, behavioral task outputs, physiological measures, or any other per-subject numeric measurement bundle for a cohort. Sidecar companion to per-subject Network sidecars in multi-subject studies that correlate simulated quantities with empirical scores (e.g. PMAT24_A, g-factor, CardSort, ProcSpeed for Schirner 2023). The yaml carries metadata + the measure list; the h5 carries ``measures/<name>`` 1-D float arrays of length ``len(subjects)``. Per-measure metadata can optionally carry Cognitive Atlas (https://www.cognitiveatlas.org/) ``cogat:Task`` and ``cogat:Concept`` IRIs via ``measure_specs``.

ProcedureStepc back to ToC or Class ToC

A single named step (or output) in a Procedure: one typed operation producing one named intermediate. `type` selects the operation and therefore which of the fields below apply; it defaults to `equation`, the general case, so a Procedure written purely as equations needs no type annotations. PropagationGatec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/PropagationGate

A propagation requirement on a grouped wave reduction. A per-timestep wave test cannot tell a standing field from a travelling one, since a standing field repeats the same spatial pattern every timestep. The reduction sums the per-element unit direction vector over the post-transient timesteps and computes each group's direction dispersion, the ``mask``-weighted mean over elements of 1 - |time-mean direction|: 0 for a direction field fixed in time, growing as the direction moves. A group whose dispersion falls below ``min_dispersion`` has no travelling waves, so its proportion of waves is 0 and its proportion-directed and rho are undefined (NaN).
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

Provenancec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Provenance

W3C PROV-O aligned provenance ABOUT the artifact that carries it — reusable on any entity (Network, TimeSeries, Dynamics, ...), which is why it holds no identity of its own: the parent supplies that. The identified ``prov:Entity`` a standalone provenance record names is ``ResultEntity``, which carries one of these. Carried by the frozen spec beside a result container, this is the whole record of the run: ``activities`` says what was executed and when, ``environment`` says on what machine and against which package versions, and ``digest`` checksums what came out. None of that is derivable from a recipe, which is why it is recorded — and all of it travels with the artifact it describes rather than in a parallel directory that has to be kept in step.

Reducerc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Reducer

A streaming reduction, authored as symbolic recurrences over its own state rather than as backend code. Folded into the integrator carry so a windowed observable (a sliding-window FC, a running mean) is computed without ever materialising the trajectory. `add` folds an arriving sample in, `evict` takes a leaving one back out, `resync` rebuilds the state exactly from the window when incremental drift would accumulate, and `emit` reads the reduced value out. TVBO lowers all four through the sympy printers, so no backend ships a reducer and adding one is a YAML file rather than code.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

A small typed pointer to another TVBO entity (Network, Mesh, Observation, …). ResultBindingc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/ResultBinding

One entry in a study's results manifest: a manuscript key bound to the value it stands for. Exactly one of three forms: COMPUTED FROM A RUN — ``used:`` a DataRef reading a scalar out of a nested study's or this study's own analysis/experiment, formatted through ``format`` — COMPUTED FROM THE SPEC — ``count:`` a structural tally of a collection (e.g. the figures a nested study regenerates), needing no run — or AUTHORED — a literal ``value`` quoted from prior work and attributed by ``source``. So a number printed in prose is computed or an authored constant marked as such, never transcribed by hand.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

ResultEntityc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/ResultEntity

One persisted result container, described. The ``prov:Entity`` of BEP028's ``prov-<label>_ent`` record: what the file is, what produced it, and what it holds. Every field is either a pointer or read off the artifact when it is written — nothing here restates a value the frozen spec beside the container already carries, which is what made the earlier curated JSON sidecar drift from the YAML next to it. Named for the entity rather than for the experiment because an analysis container (``ana-<name>_result.h5``) gets one too, and because the in-memory ``tvbo.data.types.ExperimentResult`` is a different thing: the arrays themselves, not the description of the file holding them.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

Each stage keeps its own best iterate and restores it before the next stage starts, so every stage restarts from the best state the previous one found; the run records one iteration and value per stage. StateSelectionc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/StateSelection

Which iterate of an online tuning run hands its parameters to the post-tuning evaluation and to the algorithms that depend on it. Absent, the final iterate does. Declared, the loop keeps the tuned parameters and the settled state of the iteration whose criterion was best, tracked across every stage jointly and restored after the last stage (or per stage under `scope: stage`); the run records the chosen iteration and its criterion value. This is the published feedback-inhibition simulator's practice of keeping the weights of the iteration with the lowest in-loop FC error rather than the last ones.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

Themec back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/Theme

A project's whole look in one declarable object: its colours (inherited from `Palette`), the geometry a style sheet used to own — tick shape, axis weight, line weights, legend, grid, type — and the rule its axes follow: who places the ticks, where an axis ends, which spines are drawn and whether they meet. Declared on a study (`SimulationStudy.theme`) it is the one rule every figure of that study is drawn by; declared on a figure it states only that figure's differences. Either way it beats every layer in `Figure.style`, so a look a spec states cannot be quietly overridden by a sheet underneath it. It is the reason a study need not ship a `.mplstyle`: a sheet is a backend's vocabulary written outside the spec, where nothing validates it and no other backend can read it. TVB-O's own is curated at `tvbo:themes/default`; a project names that in `iri` and states only what it changes, exactly as an `Observation` or a `Coupling` reuses a curated one. A slot left unset is not a value — the layer underneath keeps it, so a theme states the look it means to fix and nothing else.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Document c, Palette c
has members
bsplot ni, default ni

https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

volume (PanelKind)c back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/PanelKind#volume

A layer's per-region values painted into a labelled volume and projected as a glass brain — the volumetric counterpart of `surface`, and how a paper shows a whole-brain map without committing to a cortical mesh. Geometry and the label lookup come from a curated atlas (`atlas:`, whose companion dseg carries one integer label per region) or a segmentation file (`volume:`); values are placed BY LABEL through the atlas terminology, never by array position, so a region's value cannot land on its neighbour. Camera via opts (view, intensity_projection), colour via cmap/symmetric/percentile/vmin/vmax. Needs no code_modules — the drawing is built in.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
PanelKind c

WorkflowConfigc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/WorkflowConfig

Declarative orchestration for rendering a parameter sweep into a distributed, reproducible workflow (Slurm array, Snakemake, Nextflow). Backend- and engine-independent: it names *what* to distribute, *where* results go, and the per-engine resources, while each engine emitter renders the concrete artefact. Declared on a study as ``workflow`` and refined per experiment via ``workflow_overrides``; unset fields fall back to the emitter's defaults so an override sets only what it names.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

WorkflowDistributeByc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/WorkflowDistributeBy

Default tier a sweep axis is placed on when it is not named explicitly in a DistributionConfig. Vectorized axes are packed into one batched backend call; workflow axes are fanned out into independent scheduler tasks.

WorkflowEngineConfigc back to ToC or Class ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/WorkflowEngineConfig

Execution directives for a workflow engine. Every field is optional and each engine's emitter consumes the subset it supports, so one block may carry directives for more than one target. The generic resource fields (cpus_per_task, mem, time) map across engines; the remaining fields are named for the engine that reads them (Slurm: partition/account/gres/ mail_*/array_chunk; Snakemake: cores; Nextflow: executor/queue). Any directive not named here is passed through ``options`` verbatim, so the block stays extensible without a schema change.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has super-classes
Thing c

analyses (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/analyses

Analyses of this study's results, each persisted as its own container and so bindable by a figure or a later analysis exactly like a run. These take the ``Analysis`` form that invokes a ``callable`` over ``arguments`` (the ``type``/``target``/``wrt`` form analyses a solve and belongs on an ``Observation`` instead), and each needs a unique ``name`` — it keys the container. An argument's ``used:`` DataRef both records what was consumed and orders the run: ``tvbo run`` executes the analyses around the experiments — one an experiment consumes first, one consuming an experiment after — and then renders the figures.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

animation (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/animation

Turns the figure into a movie over one dimension of its data instead of a still. Every other field keeps its meaning — the mosaic, the panels, the sizing and the styling are the frame; the animation only says which dimension advances and how fast. Declaring it is what makes a figure whose subject is a *process* show the process rather than a snapshot of it, without a second, hand-written plotting path.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

batch_mode (study)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/study/batch_mode

How the per-subject fits are executed. ``fan_out`` (default) runs one per-subject job, each binding its own targets at run time. ``on_device`` evaluates the whole cohort together as one vectorised batch on a single device — the subject axis mapped in parallel while the shared network is reused across subjects. Backend-independent intent: the scientific spec is identical either way; only the execution strategy differs (a backend realises the batch with its own vectorised-map primitive).
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

correlated_over (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/correlated_over

Which axis `covariance` indexes — `node` (equivalently `region`) for spatially correlated drive, or `state` for correlation between the noise on different state variables. Required whenever `covariance` is set: a covariance without a named axis does not identify a process. A multi-mode model carries its modes inside the state axis, so a modal covariance is declared over `state`.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

coupling_evaluation (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/coupling_evaluation

Backend-neutral numerical treatment of the network coupling term across the stages of a multi-stage integrator (Heun, RK4, ...): re-evaluated at every stage (per_stage, standard ODE accuracy) or computed once per step and held across the stages (per_step, the TVB scheme). A single-stage method (Euler) and a single node integrate the same system under both. tvboptim's native solvers, NetworkDynamics.jl and the jax backend honour both values, the jax backend per_stage over an undelayed coupling only; TVB and the Python graph runner integrate per_step and refuse per_stage, and tvboptim's diffrax solvers and PyRates always integrate per_stage, whatever is declared (CouplingStageEvaluation states each value's behaviour). per_stage is required to match reference integrators for stiff, chaotic or multistable systems, where the frozen-coupling error can select a different trajectory or attractor.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

coupling_function (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

covariance (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/covariance

Covariance of the unit-intensity noise increment across the axis named by `correlated_over` — the second-order structure of the driving process, stated as mathematics rather than as a factorisation. Must be square in that axis, symmetric and positive semi-definite; its diagonal carries per-element variances and need NOT be unity, so unequal variances and cross-element correlation are expressed together. The realised increment is the declared sigma times a draw from this covariance, so `parameters: {sigma: ...}` continues to mean what it means for uncorrelated noise. Absent (the default) means the increment is independent across that axis. Being a `Parameter`, it carries the full provenance triple: a literal `value:`, existing bytes via `source:`+`measure:`, or — the usual case for a derived operator — `producer:`, whose FunctionCall records how the structure was obtained (projecting a spatially white field into a modal basis, spreading independent per-region drives through a connectome). The generative account therefore lives in the provenance, and the matrix itself stays a statement about the process. How a backend samples it (Cholesky, eigendecomposition, whitening) is a backend concern and is never stated here.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

evict_equation (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/evict_equation

Optional reverse recurrence for a **sliding-window** reduction: the per-step downdate that removes the sample leaving the window, the inverse of ``equation`` (which folds an arriving sample in). Only meaningful when ``equation_type: recurrence`` on an observation's auxiliary ``dynamics``. When present, the observer is a windowed reduction — its state is maintained by ``equation`` (add) and ``evict_equation`` (evict) and rebuilt exactly from the window on resync — rather than a cumulative accumulator over the whole trajectory (``equation`` alone). Absent for ordinary state variables and cumulative reductions.

Default Node attributes applied to every Node in this Network. Explicit entries in `nodes:` override the template field-by-field (shallow replace, same semantics as `dict.update`). noise_draw (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/noise_draw

How the base solve draws its noise realization, and therefore WHICH realization it is: `fused` draws the whole [n_steps, ...] tensor in one call, `blocked` regenerates each block of `block_size` steps from (key, block_index). Those are different draws from the same seed, so the grain is a declared property of the integration rather than something inferred from how the run is consumed. An observable declared `reduce: streaming` folds block by block whatever this says, because a reduction has no trajectory to fold otherwise; declare `blocked` to put the whole run on that same grain.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

part (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/part

Which part of a generated report this belongs in — the main Methods or the supplementary material. Placement only: every experiment runs and every figure renders regardless, so demoting one never changes what is computed. It answers a different question from a replication's target tier (how central a claim is) and from the source paper's own Fig/EDF numbering (where *they* printed it), because our document may carry a headline result's parameter dump in the SI, or relegate a figure the paper printed up front. producer (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/producer

HOW to compute this value, when it is derived rather than obtained — the callable that produces it, its arguments, and (via `output:`) which entry to take from a callable returning several named arrays. The callable resolves against the recipe's `code_source`. Use instead of `source:` for a value that is a deterministic function of the spec's own inputs (a mesh operator, a template matrix): declaring the producer keeps the spec the single source of truth, where pointing at a pre-built file would let the two drift apart silently — and would need a prep step run by hand before the spec could execute. The result is cached and invalidated by the artifact fingerprint, so it is computed once rather than per run. On a `Parameter` it produces the value; on an `Edge` it produces the whole template matrix, which is what lets a connectome or a discrete differential operator be declared rather than pre-built. Mutually exclusive with `value:`/`source:`.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
has range
FunctionCall c

studies (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/studies

Other studies this one aggregates, each a ``SimulationStudy`` in its own right — so a study-of-studies is the same class as the studies it holds, and nesting recurses to any depth without a wrapper class standing between a study and the studies it holds. A whole manuscript is then one runnable specification whose sub-studies are runnable specifications. Written as ``!include <path>`` so each sub-study keeps its own recipe file and therefore its own directory: its ``code_source``, its results root and its relative references all resolve against where it lives, not against whoever included it. ``tvbo run`` walks the nested studies depth first, then runs the owning study's own experiments, analyses and figures — the paper-native content belonging to no sub-study. Legitimized by COMBINE/OMEX, SED-ML and the ISA ``Investigation`` top-level container it parallels.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

subnetwork (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/subnetwork

Optional finer-scale Network that "lives inside" this Node (network-of-networks / multi-scale primitive). The subnetwork's nodes map (one-to-many) to this single parent Node. Cross-scale signal flow is declared as ordinary Edges in the subnetwork's `edges` list, using `source_network` / `target_network` with the `parent` sentinel to traverse up the hierarchy. The subnetwork may carry its own `graph_generator` (discrete sub-network — reservoir, spiking population, jaxley compartments) and/or `mesh` (continuous surface field) — one unified slot for reservoirs-per-region, spiking-populations-per-region, cells-per-region, and surface-mesh-patches-per-region. Recursive: a subnetwork's Nodes can themselves carry subnetworks.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

Network c

sweep_direction (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/sweep_direction

Order in which a branch-following axis (sweep_seeding: from_previous) is traversed: 'up' increases the parameter once, 'down' decreases it once, 'bidirectional' increases then decreases over the same values and records both branches — a hysteresis loop where they differ. Ignored when sweep_seeding is 'independent'. Applies to a single swept axis.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

sweep_seeding (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/sweep_seeding

How each sweep point's initial state is obtained. 'independent' (default) cold-starts every point from the model's initial values, so points are order-independent and may run in parallel (see parallel_mode). 'from_previous' seeds each point from the final state of the preceding point, so the trajectory follows the solution branch as the swept parameter changes quasi-statically; this forces sequential execution (a scan, not a vmap) and, with sweep_direction, exposes hysteresis / multistability. It is forward-integration branch following, not numerical continuation (cf. the Continuation class).
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

Unit of every time-valued number in this scope — the step size, any period, and the physical meaning of one model time-step. Declared at whichever scope owns the clock (network, integrator, observation); `tvbo.utils.units.time_unit_of` resolves a scope to its effective unit by walking outwards, and states the `ms` fallback once, at the end of that walk. Deliberately carries no default: a defaulted slot cannot be inherited through, so `ifabsent: ms` made an unset unit indistinguishable from one someone wrote, and masked an explicitly declared `s` one scope out. `time_scale` is accepted as a synonym.

transforms (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/transforms

Ordered list of transforms applied to edge property matrices. Each entry rewrites the edge property its `output:` names, else the one its `name:` is (e.g. 'weight', 'length'), and that property is also the value under transform inside the entry's own equation, which is written over the network's edge attributes. Supports equation-based (symbolic) or callable-based (software) transforms. Multiple transforms on the same target are applied sequentially, each seeing the previous one's output; since `name:` identifies an entry, each after the first states the target as its `output:`.

weight_parameter (slot)op back to ToC or Object Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/weight_parameter

Per-node stimulus weighting supplied as a Parameter, so a DERIVED weighting carries its provenance instead of being inlined as a list of numbers. Use it when the weighting is measured or computed rather than hand-listed: `source:` + `measure:` names the stored array, `producer:` names the call that builds it (an ROI mask projected through a basis, a retinotopic map, a measured stimulation field). This is the same provenance triple every other external array uses, so a spatial stimulus pattern is described by where it came from rather than by a literal a reader cannot check. Resolved at load time into the per-node `weights`, aligned with `nodes` exactly as a literal weighting is; mutually exclusive with `weight_distribution`, and a literal `weights` wins over both.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

newton_tol (slot)dp back to ToC or Data Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/newton_tol

Absolute tolerance on the residual at which the Newton corrector has converged: the norm of the right-hand side f(x, p) at the corrected point must fall below it, in the units of f. BifurcationKit.jl applies it as that bound (NewtonPar tol). AUTO-07p tests the size of each Newton correction instead, relative to the size of the solution, so the AUTO-07p backends (auto-07p and pyrates-bifurcation) set both of its relative criteria to it, EPSL on the parameter and EPSU on the state, and only approximate the residual bound: a correction and the residual it removes differ by the conditioning of the Jacobian. Unset, each backend keeps its own default, BifurcationKit.jl 1e-12 on the residual and AUTO-07p 1e-7 on the correction. A branch's nested continuation that leaves it unset takes its parent's.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

system_size (slot)dp back to ToC or Data Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/system_size

System size (van Kampen Ω) for the stochastic 'gillespie' backend: the number of discrete units per unit of the activity variable, and the sole source of noise. Runs a mean-field rate model as a finite birth-death process (Gillespie SSA): the activity state variable X becomes a discrete count n ≈ Ω·X, its relaxation equation tau*X' = -X + F(...) is read as birth propensity Ω·F/tau (the gain) and death propensity n/tau (the leak), while the remaining state variables integrate deterministically between events. Larger Ω means finer discreteness and weaker fluctuations, recovering the deterministic mean field as Ω→∞. For an activity already expressed as a fraction in [0,1], Ω is the population size N; for a firing rate it is N divided by the rate at full activation. Required by the 'gillespie' backend; ignored by every other backend.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

tail_duration (slot)dp back to ToC or Data Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/tail_duration

The trailing span of simulated time to aggregate over, in the same time unit as the integration step. Converted to a sample count against the spacing of the samples it is cut from, so the window stays the same length of simulated time at any step: this observation's own sample period (its `period`/`downsample_period`, else the integration `step_size`) for a recorded trajectory, and the integration `step_size` for a `reduce: streaming` reducer or a tuning loop, which fold every step. On an algorithm's observation the span may cover several iterations: a duration longer than the algorithm's `simulation_period` must be a whole multiple of it, and the observation is then the mean over that many most recent periods, or over every period so far while fewer have run. Mutually exclusive with `tail_samples`.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

tail_x (slot)dp back to ToC or Data Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/tail_x

Start the arrow at this x in DATA coordinates instead of at an axes-fraction offset. Pair with tail_used, which supplies the y: together they anchor the arrow's tail on a point the run computed, so a callout keeps pointing at its data when the data changes. Ignored unless tail_used is also set.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl

transient_time (slot)dp back to ToC or Data Property ToC

IRI: https://w3id.org/tvbo/transient_time

Length of the leading settling window, prepended to `duration`. It marks part of ONE integration — never a separate simulation: the backend integrates `transient_time + duration` in a single scan and the marked head is cut where the run is consumed (observations, analyses, plots, saved data), so the settle is in-band for any observation kernel that needs warm-up. Time is measured from the START of the measured window: the settle carries non-positive timestamps and ends at 0, the measured window opens one step later, and a declared event `t0` is relative to measurement, never to the scan. A settle that a fit reuses across many candidate evaluations is NOT this slot — that is a seed, declared as `initial_state.method: time_integration` with its own `duration`.
Is defined by
https://w3id.org/tvbo/tvbo.owl
